KPCC president B.K. Hariprasad said party spokesperson Kripa Alva would be asked to explain her alleged involvement in the sting operation. | Photo Credit: MURALI KUMAR K
The alleged sting operation targeting former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah took a fresh turn on Friday with his son and Urban Development Minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah alleging that a Congress woman leader aspiring for a party ticket to contest the Assembly elections was involved.
Speaking to reporters in Mysuru on Friday, Mr. Yathindra claimed the woman leader was keen on securing a Congress ticket to contest from the Puttur Assembly constituency in Dakshina Kannada district. He alleged that she had joined hands with the head of a media organisation to carry out the sting operation.
Though Mr. Yathindra did not name either the Congress leader or the media representative, Mr. Siddaramaiah later identified the woman as Krupa Alva and the media representative as Rakesh Shetty, owner of Power TV, while speaking to reporters.
Mr. Yathindra said an investigation was necessary to establish whether the Congress leader and the media representative had acted on their own or whether others were behind the episode. However, he clarified that the alleged involvement of an individual party worker did not mean that the Congress was against Mr. Siddaramaiah.
Mr. Yathindra said his father had spoken to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Home Minister Priyank Kharge to ensure a proper investigation and the arrest of those responsible.
Soon after, KPCC president B.K. Hariprasad said here that a show-cause notice would be issued to Ms. Alva, who is KPCC spokesperson, seeking an explanation for her alleged role in the episode.
Congress sources said the party was considering expelling her for embarrassing the government and giving the Opposition ammunition to target it. Ms. Alva had served as the chairperson of the Karnataka State Commission for Protection of Child Rights during the first term of the Siddaramaiah government in 2015.
Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel H.D. Kumaraswamy, who held a press conference on Friday, alleged that Mr. Shetty and Ms. Alva had played a key role in orchestrating the alleged sting operation against Mr. Siddaramaiah. He alleged that the entire episode was the result of internal political rivalry within the Congress, demanding to know who the “kingpin” was.
Home Minister Priyank Kharge stated on Friday that some people “who want to climb the ladder” may be behind the purported sting operation targeting former Chief Minister Siddarmaiah, but no senior Congress leaders had any role in it. Some people who have aspirations to be MLA, MLC or chairperson or a board or a corporation may be involved, he indicated.
On the demand for SIT probe, he said, “Mr. Siddaramaiah has clearly stated that the investigation is progressing well and that there is no need for the SIT. Our officers are capable of handling the case, and the investigation is proceeding as planned. Mr. Siddaramaiah is fully aware of the procedures and the progress made so far. It is only a matter of time before the facts emerge.”
